<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #25999 

Problem Summary:
Insert succeeded with values out-of-range for Timestamp

### What is changed and how it works?
Never accept timestamp values out-of-range

What's Changed:
Check for values out-of-range

How it Works:
Now truncates and returns a warning or returns an error depending on sql_mode.

Side effects

Documentation

- [ ] Contains syntax changes
- [ ] Contains variable changes
- [ ] Contains experimental features

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->
```release-note
Timestamp values out-of-range can no longer be inserted.
```

Update: I didn't reproduce it because I used TiDB with Unistore(mocktikv), it is reproducible with TiDB + TiKV.

So the root cause is 'TiDB failed to validate the data, while TiKV did the validation'.

review_comments: Could remove the field of `InReorgAttribute` in SC? It seems to be used only for `KindMysqlTime`.
Good catch! Thank you for spotting it, I have removed it (basically this PR will replace https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/26395 apart from the added tests).
Do we need to check the sql_mode here? Is this covered by tests?

This change was needed (detected) by TestIssue23609, I don't think it should have different behaviour depending on sql_mode (as I understand it, this is an equal match/lookup so if there is an invalid timestamp, it cannot find a match).

In my MySQL8.0, I executed the above statements, it returned the warning of `Out of range`. That's not consistent with the tests.
```
mysql> SET @@sql_mode='';
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.01 sec)

mysql> CREATE TABLE ts (id int DEFAULT NULL, time1 TIMESTAMP NULL DEFAULT NULL);
Query OK, 0 rows affected (0.07 sec)

mysql> INSERT INTO ts (id, time1) VALUES (1, TIMESTAMP '1018-12-23 00:00:00') ;
Query OK, 1 row affected, 1 warning (0.02 sec)

mysql> show warnings;
+---------+------+------------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                        |
+---------+------+------------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1264 | Out of range value for column 'time1' at row 1 |
+---------+------+------------------------------------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)

mysql> select version();
+-----------+
| version() |
+-----------+
| 8.0.25    |
+-----------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

Yes, TiDB handling of out-of-range differs from MySQL.
Here is an example for `int` instead of `timestamp`:
TiDB:
```sql
tidb> CREATE TABLE t1 (
  id int NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  ts timestamp NULL DEFAULT NULL
);
tidb> INSERT INTO t1 (id, ts) VALUES (2147483648, TIMESTAMP '2018-12-23 00:00:00');
Query OK, 1 row affected, 1 warning (0,00 sec)
tidb> SHOW WARNINGS;
+---------+------+-----------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                           |
+---------+------+-----------------------------------+
| Warning | 1690 | constant 2147483648 overflows int |
+---------+------+-----------------------------------+
1 row in set (0,00 sec)
```
MySQL:
```sql
mysql> INSERT INTO t1 (id, ts) VALUES (2147483648, TIMESTAMP '2018-12-23 00:00:00');
Query OK, 1 row affected, 1 warning (0,01 sec)
mysql> SHOW WARNINGS
+---------+------+---------------------------------------------+
| Level   | Code | Message                                     |
+---------+------+---------------------------------------------+
| Warning | 1264 | Out of range value for column 'id' at row 1 |
+---------+------+---------------------------------------------+
```

@zimulala I think fixing these differences is outside of the scope for this bug. Do you want me to create a new issue for the mysql incompatibility?
I think we can file an issue first.
